articles.title: Ubisoft posts a €254.5 million half-year loss and spins out a generative AI studio
articles.dek: Net bookings fell 16.5% in the six months to September, headcount dropped by about 1,100, and Ubisoft confirmed Motherbrain as a dedicated subsidiary for AI in gameplay.
facts: Down close to 1,100 in six months
Net bookings down high single digits
articles.body:
Ubisoft's first-half results show a publisher still shrinking while it reorganizes. In the six months to September 30, net bookings came to €644.7 million, down 16.5% from €772.4 million a year earlier. The second quarter alone brought in €388.9 million, a 20.8% drop, though Ubisoft noted that was ahead of its own guidance of around €370 million.
The bottom line got worse. The IFRS net loss attributable to shareholders widened to €254.5 million from €161.3 million, and the IFRS operating loss grew to €189.2 million.
## Fewer people, smaller costs
Ubisoft says its headcount fell by close to 1,100 over the half and its fixed cost base dropped 6% to €660 million. The results arrived the same week Ubisoft announced 166 more layoffs in Montreal and Quebec City. It ended September with about €1.03 billion in cash, and says it used cash in mid-November to settle a €453 million convertible bond that holders chose to redeem early. A two-part refinancing plan is underway.
## Motherbrain becomes its own company
The report also confirms Motherbrain as a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay. CEO Yves Guillemot described it as the team behind Teammates, the experimental generative AI project Ubisoft showed in late 2025, which uses AI-driven characters that respond to players. According to VGC, it is not yet clear whether Motherbrain's work will ship as standalone products or be built into other Ubisoft games. Ubisoft says its new operating model, which began rolling out in January alongside six game cancellations, is now fully in place.
## What's next
Ubisoft kept its full-year targets: net bookings down by a high single-digit percentage, a negative non-IFRS operating margin, and free cash outflow of no more than €500 million. It expects around €250 million in third-quarter net bookings, with Rayman Legends Retold and Just Dance: Decades of Hits among this quarter's releases. Rainbow Six Tactics and the Heroes of Might and Magic III remake are slated for 2027.

articles.title: GTA VI's Japanese version tones down nudity and blood
articles.dek: Players in Japan found swimsuits in the shower, less gore and no way to turn it back up. Rockstar did not announce the changes ahead of launch.
facts: Nudity covered or cut, blood and gore reduced
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI players in Japan are getting a noticeably tamer game than the rest of the world, and many only found out once they started playing.
## What's different
According to Kotaku and VGC, which both cite footage and screenshots shared by Japanese players, nudity has been removed or covered throughout. Jason and Lucia wear swimwear in shower scenes, sex scenes and beach areas have been changed, and some scenes are reportedly cut altogether.
Violence is also dialed back. Japanese outlet GameSpark reports that blood from injured and dead characters is reduced, disappears faster, and that decapitations have been removed. Elsewhere, players can lower gore and switch off dismemberment in the settings, but the Japanese version offers no option to raise it. VGC says the changes appear to be cosmetic, and the missions themselves play out the same way.
## Warning signs before launch
Fans had suspected regional changes for weeks. Kotaku says the Japanese download was more than 1GB smaller than other regions, and the game's CERO rating in Japan left out the sexual content descriptors listed by rating boards elsewhere. Rockstar did not confirm any changes before release. Australian and New Zealand downloads are also slightly smaller, VGC notes, but there is no evidence yet that those versions are edited.
Kotaku also reports that the Japanese release carries only English voice acting with English and Japanese subtitles, while other regions offer more than a dozen languages but no Japanese text. Censoring Japanese releases is not new for the series, which has made similar edits in past entries.

articles.title: Digital Foundry doubts GTA VI could run on Switch 2
articles.dek: After testing the launch versions, Digital Foundry says a Switch 2 port looks extremely unlikely, with the game's CPU demands already pinning PS5 Pro to 30fps.
facts: PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S
articles.body:
Now that Grand Theft Auto VI is out, Digital Foundry has weighed in on one of the most persistent fan questions: could it ever come to Nintendo Switch 2? Its answer is a firm probably not.
## The CPU problem
In a video discussed by Nintendo Life, Digital Foundry says a Switch 2 version feels extremely unlikely at this stage. The core issue is the game's heavy CPU load. That bottleneck is why GTA VI runs at 30 frames per second even on PS5 Pro, a machine with far more processing power than Nintendo's hybrid.
Digital Foundry's John Linneman said that without major changes he could not see how the game would work on Switch 2.
## Series S already struggles
The weakest current version offers a hint of the challenge. Digital Foundry describes Xbox Series S performance as compromised, with frame rates often sitting in the mid to high 20s during normal play. The Series S is generally considered more capable than Switch 2 in raw CPU terms, so a Nintendo port would need deeper cuts than resolution alone.
## No plans announced
Rockstar has not announced any version beyond PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and has not dated a PC release. Earlier Rockstar games did eventually reach Nintendo hardware, but those ports arrived years after launch and on games that were far less demanding. For now, Switch 2 owners should not expect a trip to Leonida.

articles.title: Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable start to finish, and Chapter 7 work has begun
articles.dek: Toby Fox's fall newsletter says Chapter 6 is a structurally complete draft heading into localization, though some scenes still need work before full testing.
articles.body:
Deltarune creator Toby Fox has shared a fresh development update, and Chapter 6 has reached a big milestone.
## Chapter 6
In his Fall 2026 newsletter, as reported by PC Gamer and Nintendo Life, Fox says Chapter 6 now exists as a structurally complete draft that can be played from beginning to end. All of its maps, events and battles are in place, with the exception of one optional event that is still in progress.
That means the team can begin localization and some preliminary testing. Full testing has to wait, though, because Fox says several important scenes and details still need more work. He also made clear he does not intend to hurry the remaining polish.
Fox has previously said Chapter 6 is aimed at 2027, and that it will be shorter and more focused on the story's central mysteries than earlier chapters.
## Chapter 7
Development on Chapter 7, the planned final chapter, has only just started, with designers who finished their Chapter 6 work moving onto it. Fox says he read some of its events and dialogue to the team but stopped at a key moment, telling them they will need to finish more of the game before they find out what happens.
## Fan vote
The newsletter also settled a community vote: Queen won with 65% of the vote, and the prize is a silly bonus scene in Chapter 6. Fox says the next update should arrive once Chapter 6's localization is done.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time stays No. 1 in Japan as Metaphor: ReFantazio debuts on Switch 2
articles.dek: The Switch 2 Zelda remake sold another 86,097 boxed copies in Japan in its second full week, while Switch 2 outsold every other console combined.
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time held the top spot in Japan's physical charts for the week of November 9 to 15, according to Famitsu data reported by Gematsu. The Switch 2 game sold 86,097 boxed copies, bringing its total to 623,138 since its November 5 launch.
## Top five
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2): 86,097
- Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2, new): 11,167
- Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (Switch 2): 11,086
- Rhythm Heaven Groove (Switch): 7,779
- Minecraft Dungeons II (Switch, new): 4,264
Atlus's fantasy RPG Metaphor: ReFantazio arrived on Switch 2 in second place, narrowly ahead of Switch Sports Resort. Pikmin 4's Switch 2 Edition with Dandori Academy also debuted, at No. 8 with 2,854 copies. Final Fantasy Resonance was the only non-Nintendo-platform game in the top 10, at No. 10 on PS5.
## Hardware
Switch 2 sold 42,402 units for the week, lifting its Japanese total past 6.6 million. That was nearly three times the combined total of every other system. The PS5 family sold 11,136, almost all of it the Digital Edition, while the original Switch family sold 3,754 and Xbox Series consoles sold 707.
These figures cover only physical retail sales in Japan and do not include digital downloads. GTA VI's November 19 launch will fall in next week's data.

articles.title: Rockstar puts GTA VI's day-one retail sales at $3.79 billion
articles.dek: Take-Two's own estimate, filed with US regulators, calls it the biggest entertainment launch ever and adds a record 32.5 million units sold before release.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive have put their own number on Grand Theft Auto VI's opening: an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on day one. The figure appeared in a press release dated November 20 that Take-Two also filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission as part of an 8-K report.
The release calls GTA VI the biggest entertainment launch in history and says it set a sales record for entertainment in any medium. It also says the game sold 32.5 million units before release, which Rockstar describes as a record across all platforms.
## How the number was counted
A footnote says the $3.79 billion is based on company estimates through the end of November 19 worldwide. The release does not split digital from physical sales or say how units are defined, so it is not directly comparable with Take-Two's quarterly net bookings, which use a different accounting basis.
The official figure is well above outside estimates published the same week. Sensor Tower had estimated about $2.36 billion and 24.6 million copies by the end of launch day, and earlier reports had put preorder revenue below $2 billion.
## What else Rockstar said
The release highlights the game's 99 Metacritic score and lists the stores carrying it: the PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store, Rockstar Games Store and retailers worldwide. GTA VI is out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced.
Rockstar president Sam Houser said the studio was "incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world." For context, the release notes that GTA V has sold in nearly 235 million units and the series nearly 480 million.
Take-Two reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 net bookings forecast of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion earlier in November.

articles.title: GTA VI's Metacritic user score sinks to 5.6 as fans start review-bombing Zelda
articles.dek: Thousands of zero scores have hit GTA VI's user page, and some GTA fans have retaliated against Ocarina of Time, which held Metacritic's top user score.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI may be the best-reviewed game on Metacritic, but its user score tells a different story. According to VGC, the game's user rating had fallen to 5.6 out of 10 from more than 10,000 reviews as of November 23, against a critic score of 99.
Metacritic held back user reviews until 36 hours after launch, its usual practice, after removing fake reviews that had been posted before the game was out. Once the page opened, a large share of the scores were zeros.
## What the low scores say
VGC reports that many of the zero-score reviews complain about the game's story, describing it as a relationship simulator built around keeping co-lead Lucia happy. Others use culture-war language to attack the game. VGC called the pattern of zero scores suspicious.
## The retaliation
Some GTA fans have responded by targeting other games at the top of Metacritic's charts. The 2026 Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which had the highest user score on the site, has received a wave of zero ratings over the past few days. Several reviewers say they are GTA fans who believe Zelda fans bombed GTA VI first.
The remake's user score was still 8.3 when VGC checked, propped up by tens of thousands of positive reviews posted after its launch. The original 1998 Ocarina of Time and SoulCalibur, third on the all-time list, have also picked up zero scores from GTA fans.
## Why it matters
User scores on Metacritic tend to cluster at zero and ten, and coordinated campaigns have pushed games up and down the lists before. The swings say more about fan rivalries than about how good any of these games are. Critic scores for both GTA VI and Ocarina of Time are unaffected.

articles.title: GTA VI gets its first post-launch patch, with no patch notes
articles.dek: Update 1.002.002 is rolling out in stages on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar hasn't said what it changes.
facts: About 604MB on PS5, 1.6GB on Xbox Series X|S
articles.body:
Rockstar has started rolling out the first Grand Theft Auto VI update since the game launched on November 19. Version 1.002.002 on PS5, listed as 1.0.2.2 on Xbox Series X|S, began reaching players on November 23.
According to Push Square and Tbreak, the download is about 604MB on PS5 and 1.6GB on Xbox Series X|S. It is the third patch in roughly ten days, following two pre-launch updates on November 13 and November 16.
## A staggered release
The update is not arriving for everyone at once. Rockstar dataminer Tex2 reported that it would reach a third of PS5 owners first, two thirds after about three hours and everyone within six hours. Push Square says the staging appears designed to avoid overloading servers. Players who don't see it yet can check for updates manually from the game's options menu on console.
## What it fixes
Rockstar has not published patch notes, and neither of the earlier updates came with any. That leaves players guessing. Some reports describe the game feeling smoother after the update, but there is no confirmation of performance changes, and Tbreak cautions that this may be a placebo effect. The game's 30fps target on consoles, including PS5 Pro, is unchanged as far as anyone knows.
Players have reported a handful of launch bugs, including a PS5 error code and an Xbox glitch that runs gameplay at double speed. It is not known whether this patch addresses either.

articles.title: Hacker group Cyberleek claims to be leaking a GTA VI development build
articles.dek: The group says it has released every file from a November Xbox build except the executable, which it is holding back on a countdown. Rockstar hasn't commented.
facts: Main executable, so the files can't be run
Take-Two has subpoenaed Discord over earlier leaks
articles.body:
A hacker group calling itself Cyberleek says it has begun releasing a development build of Grand Theft Auto VI, VGC reports. The claim surfaced on November 19, the day the game launched, and has not been confirmed by Rockstar or Take-Two.
The group's site lists a download labeled as an Xbox build, version 1.0.2.1, dated November 2026. Cyberleek says it is distributing every file by torrent except the main executable, which it says is being held back on a countdown. It has also said it could release the executable sooner if a crypto token it promotes reaches a certain value, and that a PS5 build would follow only as a fallback.
## What we know
Screenshots shared on social media appear to show files from an Xbox development build, according to VGC. Without the executable, nobody can actually run the build, and the files' authenticity has not been independently verified.
Cyberleek has spent months posting what it says is GTA VI gameplay and frames its campaign as a protest over consumer rights, including the lack of a traditional disc release. VGC reports that the group has pushed crypto donations and required them to vote in polls on what to leak next.
## Rockstar's position
Rockstar has not commented on the claimed build. Take-Two has previously described its investigation into GTA VI leaks as rapidly evolving and has filed subpoenas asking Discord for information on specific servers and users.
The claim comes days after Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the 2022 GTA VI leak, pleaded guilty in a separate case. Players should be wary of any download claiming to be a leaked build: unofficial files from anonymous sources are a common way to spread malware.

articles.title: Expedition 33's former lead writer backs the Rockstar union push
articles.dek: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen says layoff fears at Rockstar after GTA VI's record launch show developers don't share fairly in the value they create.
facts: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, former lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
articles.body:
The former lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has weighed in on the union drive at Rockstar Games, arguing that worries about layoffs after Grand Theft Auto VI's record launch point to a deeper imbalance in the industry.
In comments reported by PC Gamer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen said the people who create the value in games like GTA VI don't receive a proportionate share of it. She said she hopes the Rockstar team succeeds in unionizing. Svedberg-Yen left Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive in July.
## The backdrop
Her comments follow an op-ed in The Guardian by Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte, who wrote that there was no sign layoffs were coming but that colleagues were still anxious about their jobs. Big studios have often cut staff after a major release as they shift to post-launch support, and the past few years have seen tens of thousands of job losses across the industry.
Rockstar's UK staff are voting on union recognition, with the ballot closing on November 26. The union says about 1,600 staff are eligible to vote.
## Why her voice carries weight
Expedition 33 was one of the breakout hits of 2025, made by a small team, and Svedberg-Yen has become a prominent voice on how developers are treated and credited. Her intervention adds to a growing list of developers outside Rockstar publicly backing the vote, as GTA VI's sales figures make the gap between a game's earnings and job security for its makers hard to ignore.

articles.title: GTA VI's first patch fixes broken autosaves, stuck weather and missing phone calls
articles.dek: Update 1.002.002 now has a list of fixes attached, led by the autosave bug that cost some players progress after launch.
facts: Crashes, frozen weather, missed phone calls, stuck Wanted Levels
articles.body:
When Grand Theft Auto VI's first post-launch update arrived on November 23, it came with no explanation. A list of fixes has since surfaced, and the biggest one is the problem many players were worried about: autosaving.
According to VGC, update 1.002.002, about 603MB on PS5, fixes autosaves that weren't working correctly. Since the game launched on November 19, players have reported autosave failures, and in some cases lost save data. VGC's advice in the meantime was to pause and save manually.
## What else changes
The fixes VGC lists include:
- Several crashes
- Weather that stopped changing for long stretches of time
- Phone calls that never came through, including story calls that unlock missions
- Wanted Levels that couldn't be shaken off
- A deadlift bar at the gym that couldn't be used
- Partners who wouldn't hand over bags when selling to fences
The missing phone calls were the most disruptive of these, since a story call that never triggers can leave a player unable to progress.
## Still unclear
VGC's report doesn't say where the list came from, and Rockstar hadn't published official patch notes for this update when we first covered it. The update is rolling out in stages, so players who don't have it yet can check for it manually from the console's game menu.
There is no word yet on the other launch bugs players have reported, such as a PS5 error code and an Xbox glitch that speeds gameplay up.

articles.title: Epic drops Blueprints from Unreal Engine 6 and bets on Verse and AI
articles.dek: UE6 will launch without Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework, reversing Epic's June plan to keep both alongside the new tools for a while.
facts: Blueprints visual scripting, Actor Gameplay Framework
Epic expects AI to help convert UE5 projects
June 2026: both would coexist in UE6 Early Access and 6.0
articles.body:
Epic Games has changed its plans for Unreal Engine 6 in a way that will touch a huge number of studios. In a post on the Unreal Engine site, Epic said UE6 will not support Blueprints, the visual scripting system used across the industry, or the Actor Gameplay Framework that underpins how most Unreal games are built.
Instead, according to Game Developer, Epic is putting its weight behind Verse, its own programming language, and Scene Graph, a hierarchical way of structuring game worlds. Game Developer says both lean heavily on AI.
## A reversal from June
This is a sharp change. In June 2026, Epic said Blueprints and the Actor framework would be phased out gradually, and that they would still work alongside the new tools in UE6 Early Access and version 6.0. Now they won't be there at all.
Epic's reasoning is AI. The company says it expects AI tools to help move UE5 projects over to UE6, possibly with no manual work, and that dropping the old systems lets it ship UE6 on schedule or earlier.
## Why it matters
Blueprints is how many designers and smaller teams build games without writing much traditional code. Sandfall Interactive has said Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was almost entirely built with Blueprints, Game Developer notes.
Not everyone is convinced. Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek said on social media that his team will stick with UE5. Studios with projects in progress are likely to make the same call, at least until the conversion tools prove themselves.
The move fits Epic's broader shift toward what it calls an AI-first business model.

articles.title: GTA VI leaker Arion Kurtaj is released with a five-year order limiting his online activity
articles.dek: A week after pleading guilty, the hacker behind the 2022 Rockstar leak was released on licence with a ban on Telegram and Discord.
facts: Serious Crime Prevention Order, five years
Online activity limited, including bans on Telegram and Discord
articles.body:
The hacker who leaked Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 has been released, a week after admitting his role in the Rockstar breach. According to the BBC, as reported by VGC, Arion Kurtaj was released on licence and handed a Serious Crime Prevention Order that restricts what he can do online for five years.
The order bars him from using Telegram and Discord, among other limits. The judge reportedly described Kurtaj as very talented and told him not to let it happen again.
## How he got here
In September 2022, Kurtaj and others posted roughly an hour of footage from an early GTA VI build. It was the public's first look at the game, including the lead character Lucia, more than a year before Rockstar's own reveal. Rockstar said at the time that it was extremely disappointed.
Kurtaj was linked to the Lapsus$ hacking group. In late 2023 a judge found he posed a high risk of serious harm through hacking and ordered him held in a secure hospital. Earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and moved to a regular prison in January. He pleaded guilty on November 16, three days before GTA VI launched.
Rockstar has previously said the hack cost it $5 million to recover from, according to the BBC.
The game he leaked has since gone on to the biggest launch in entertainment history, with Take-Two estimating $3.79 billion in day-one sales.

articles.title: Activision job listing names Banjo-Kazooie among its franchises
articles.dek: A posting for a project manager on 'emerging franchises' lists Banjo-Kazooie and mentions a premium console and PC game, fuelling talk of a revival.
facts: Banjo-Kazooie, a premium console and PC title
Rare moved under Activision in Xbox's September restructure
articles.body:
Banjo-Kazooie now has a new home inside Microsoft, and Activision isn't hiding it. As VGC spotted, an Activision job listing on LinkedIn for a project manager working on emerging franchises names Banjo-Kazooie among the series the company now owns.
The listing also refers to a premium console and PC title in development. It doesn't say that game is Banjo-Kazooie, and nothing has been announced, so this is a hint rather than confirmation.
## How the bear and bird got here
In September, Xbox reshuffled its studios. Halo went to Activision, and Rare, the studio that created Banjo-Kazooie, moved under Activision too, along with Age of Empires studio World's Edge.
There has been plenty of interest in bringing the series back. In July, Toys for Bob's Lou Studdert told Kinda Funny that his studio would like to make a Banjo game. In September, series composer Grant Kirkhope said at least three studios had pitched one to Microsoft. VGC says Toys for Bob is understood to be one of them and believes Moon Studios is another, though neither has been confirmed.
The last new entry was Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts on Xbox 360, about 18 years ago.

articles.title: Shinji Mikami says he sometimes wishes AI would disappear, but uses it anyway
articles.dek: At G-STAR in South Korea, the Resident Evil creator and Shift Up's Kim Hyung-tae discussed how they use AI and where they draw the line.
articles.body:
Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami has mixed feelings about AI. Speaking on stage at G-STAR 2026 in South Korea alongside Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung-tae, Mikami said he sometimes wishes AI would vanish from the world entirely, according to Inven Global's report, relayed by VGC.
He also admitted he experiments with it. He described sketching designs in 2D, using AI to preview them in 3D, and then handing the design to a human modeller. He said he was also interested in AI's potential to get better image quality out of the same hardware.
Mikami's bigger worry is jobs. He said that in five to ten years, core development work might no longer be driven by people, and developers could lose out.
## Shift Up's line
Kim said Shift Up's artists now build the foundations of their work, with AI limited to supporting tasks like lighting tests, weathering textures and reducing polygon counts. That policy followed a backlash in July over an AI-generated Stellar Blade music video.
Kim argued that players don't care how efficient a studio is, so any time saved should go into raising quality. He said Shift Up doesn't use AI to write stories.
The two have a working relationship: Shift Up acquired Mikami's studio Unbound, a deal announced in April. Mikami founded Unbound in 2023 after leaving Tango Gameworks.

articles.title: Sony says GTA VI is the biggest launch in PlayStation history, with 39 million players on PS5
articles.dek: Sony's own figures put GTA VI at more than 39 million unique PS5 players, a PlayStation concurrent-player record and 683 million hours played in its opening days.
facts: New PlayStation record for any game
First game played on 70% activated since launch
articles.body:
Sony has put its own numbers on Grand Theft Auto VI's launch, and they are enormous. According to figures Sony shared this week, reported by GamesRadar and PC Gamer, more than 39 million unique players have played the game on PS5, making it the biggest launch in PlayStation history.
The game also set a new PlayStation record for concurrent players for any game. Players logged 683 million hours in total during the opening days, which works out at roughly 17.4 hours each.
## A boost for PS5 hardware
GTA VI was also pulling in new console owners. Sony said it was the first game played on 70% of the new PS5s activated since launch day. The company also recorded its biggest single day of newly connected PS5s outside the holiday season.
These figures cover PlayStation only. GTA VI is also out on Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar has already said the game's day-one retail sales reached $3.79 billion across all platforms.
## Other games felt it
The launch seems to have pulled players away from other big live games. Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, estimated on X that daily Call of Duty players across PlayStation, Xbox and Steam fell by about 42% after GTA VI arrived, from around 7.5 million to 4.4 million. He estimated a 28% drop for Fortnite on PlayStation and Xbox. These are analyst estimates, not official numbers from Activision or Epic.

articles.title: CD Projekt says Witcher 4 is planned for 2028 and Cyberpunk 2 is making good progress
articles.dek: On its Q3 earnings call, CD Projekt compared the jump to Witcher 4 with the jump from GTA 5 to GTA 6, and said it wants shorter gaps between its RPGs.
facts: Not yet in full production; no date
About 200 by end of 2026, about 320 by end of 2027
No material impact expected on Q4
articles.body:
CD Projekt used its third-quarter earnings call on November 24 to update investors on its next two big RPGs, according to reports from PC Gamer and GamesRadar.
## The Witcher 4
Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski said the leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 would be comparable to the one from GTA 5 to GTA 6, pointing out that 11 years will have passed between the games. PC Gamer reports that The Witcher 4 is planned for 2028.
## Cyberpunk 2
Karolina Gnaś, CD Projekt's VP of strategy and investor relations, said the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel is making good progress but is not yet in full production, so it is too early to talk about a release date. PC Gamer says the game is not expected before 2030. The team is expected to grow to about 200 developers by the end of 2026 and about 320 by the end of 2027.
## Shorter waits
The studio said it plans to run several productions in parallel, some of them with external teams, so that fans don't have to wait as long between its games in future.
Asked about Grand Theft Auto VI, Nowakowski said he doesn't expect Rockstar's launch to have a material impact on CD Projekt's fourth quarter.

articles.title: Lords of the Fallen II slips to April 2027, with an exact date coming in December
articles.dek: CI Games' CEO says the soulslike sequel now launches in April 2027. It's the game's second delay, after an earlier move to the first quarter of 2027.
articles.body:
Lords of the Fallen II has been pushed back again. CI Games CEO Marek Tyminski posted that the soulslike sequel will launch in April 2027, and said the exact release date will be announced in December, GamesRadar reports.
The game was first announced at Gamescom Opening Night Live in 2025 with a release planned for the second half of 2026. In June, it moved to the first quarter of 2027. April is a further slip of at least a few weeks.
No reason for the latest delay was given in the announcement, and CI Games didn't use it to confirm the game's platforms.
The sequel follows 2023's Lords of the Fallen, a reboot of CI Games' soulslike series.
We'll add the exact date to our release radar once CI Games announces it next month.

articles.title: Capcom is shutting down Exoprimal, with servers closing in September 2027
articles.dek: Capcom's online dinosaur shooter will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027, and become unplayable when its servers go offline on September 29, 2027.
articles.body:
Capcom has announced the end of Exoprimal, its online team shooter about fighting hordes of dinosaurs in exosuits, GamesRadar reports.
The game will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. Its servers will shut down on September 29, 2027, and because Exoprimal has no offline or single-player mode, it will not be playable at all after that date.
The paid premium tiers of the Survival Pass have already been taken out of the in-game store.
## A short life
Exoprimal launched in 2023 and was available on Game Pass at release. Capcom stopped adding new content after Season 4 in 2024, so the shutdown doesn't come as a big surprise to the players who stayed.
The announcement gives players almost a full year of play before the lights go out. Anyone thinking of buying it to try has until the end of March 2027.
It's another reminder of how fragile online-only games are. Once the servers are gone, there's no way to play what you paid for.

articles.title: GTA VI tops the UK boxed chart even though the box has no disc
articles.dek: GTA VI's code-in-a-box edition entered the UK physical chart at No. 1, pushing the Ocarina of Time remake down to third, as Black Friday deals lifted older PS5 games.
facts: Download code in a box, no disc
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI has gone straight to No. 1 on the UK's boxed games chart, according to GfK data reported by Nintendo Life and Games Asylum. That's despite the fact that the physical edition doesn't contain a disc. It's a download code in a box.
Amazon UK alone reportedly sold more than 40,000 copies of the PS5 code-in-a-box edition.
## The top 10
- 1. Grand Theft Auto VI
- 2. EA Sports FC 27
- 3. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
- 4. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
- 5. Switch Sports Resort
- 6. Marvel's Wolverine
- 7. Mario Kart World
- 8. Minecraft
- 9. Onimusha: Way of the Sword
- 10. Elden Ring
The Ocarina of Time remake has now fallen for three weeks in a row since its launch-week top spot. Marvel's Wolverine jumped from 18th to sixth, and Elden Ring re-entered the top 10.
## Black Friday helps PlayStation
Early Black Friday discounts gave a lift to several older PlayStation games. Gran Turismo 7, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Cyberpunk 2077, Astro Bot and Ghost of Yotei all climbed into the lower half of the top 20.
The only new release in the top 40 besides GTA VI was The Grinch 2: Saving Christmas, at No. 40.
The UK boxed chart only counts physical sales, so it misses the large share of GTA VI copies bought digitally.

articles.title: Nioh 3's final DLC arrives early on December 17, and the series comes to Xbox in January
articles.dek: Koei Tecmo moved Nioh 3's Bloody Insurrection DLC up from February to December 17, and Nioh 3 Complete Edition launches on Xbox Series X|S on January 28.
facts: Yes, after nearly a decade on PlayStation
articles.body:
Koei Tecmo and Team Ninja have pulled Nioh 3's last expansion forward. Bloody Insurrection, the second and final DLC for the game, now launches on December 17, 2026 instead of February, GamesRadar reports.
## Nioh comes to Xbox
The bigger news for some players is a new platform. Nioh 3 Complete Edition, which bundles the base game with its DLC, launches on January 28, 2027. It's coming to Xbox Series X|S as well as PS5 and PC.
That makes it the first time a Nioh game has been released on Xbox. The series has been on PlayStation, and later PC, for almost a decade since the first game arrived in 2017.
Koei Tecmo didn't give a price for the DLC in the announcement.
The move fits a wider pattern of Japanese action games that used to be PlayStation console exclusives turning up on Xbox. We've added the DLC date to our release radar.

articles.title: PlayStation creator Ken Kutaragi says console prices are not healthy and consoles may not be needed
articles.dek: In an interview with The Game Business, Kutaragi blamed costly graphics hardware and RAM shortages for high prices, and floated a lightweight platform that isn't a console or phone.
facts: Ken Kutaragi, creator of the PlayStation
President and CEO, Cyber AI Entertainment
Expensive GPUs and RAM shortages tied partly to AI
articles.body:
Ken Kutaragi, the engineer who led the creation of the original PlayStation, thinks the console business is heading somewhere uncomfortable. In an interview with The Game Business, reported by GamesRadar, he described current console prices as not a healthy situation.
Kutaragi, who is now president and CEO of Cyber AI Entertainment, pointed to the cost of high-end graphics hardware and to RAM shortages, which he partly linked to demand from the AI industry.
## PC-like consoles
He said Sony and Microsoft moving their consoles to PC-like architecture has made it easier to release games on several platforms, but it has also pushed hardware costs up.
Looking ahead, Kutaragi suggested a time may come when dedicated consoles aren't needed. He floated the idea of a lightweight platform that is neither a traditional console nor a smartphone, though he didn't describe a specific product.
Kutaragi made clear that his comments were his own and not the views of Sony Interactive Entertainment, which he left many years ago.
His remarks come in a year when rising component costs have pushed up the price of new hardware, including Valve's warning that Steam Machine prices may rise.

articles.title: Mario Kart World update 1.9.0 adds eight tracks, all sequels to classic courses
articles.dek: Fans have nicknamed Mario Kart World's latest Switch 2 patch the update of 2s: its eight new tracks are all second versions of existing courses, plus two Knockout Tour routes.
articles.body:
Nintendo has released version 1.9.0 of Mario Kart World on Switch 2, and fans have quickly nicknamed it the update of 2s, GamesRadar reports. All eight new tracks are sequel versions of courses from earlier Mario Kart games.
## The new tracks
The additions include:
- Airship Fortress 2
- Desert Hills 2
- DK Pass 2
- Mario Bros. Circuit 2
- Koopa Troopa Beach 2
- Salty Salty Speedway 2
- Wario Stadium 2
GamesRadar's report didn't name the eighth track.
## Other changes
The update also adds two new Knockout Tour routes, Feather Rally and Lucky Cat Rally. Results screens now get confetti, and the river route to Cheep Cheep Falls can now be reached from five more courses.
Fan reaction has been mixed. Some players are happy to see more content, while others wanted brand-new courses rather than follow-ups to old ones.
The patch follows September's 1.8.0 update, which added 10 tracks from the SNES era. A larger 2.0 update is expected later.

articles.title: Team Cherry sets 'Cherry Time' showcase for November 27 with a Silksong: Sea of Sorrow update
articles.dek: The Hollow Knight studio will stream announcements on Friday, including news on Silksong's free expansion, which was promised for 2026.
facts: Hollow Knight: Silksong – Sea of Sorrow
articles.body:
Team Cherry will hold its own showcase, called Cherry Time, on Friday, November 27. The small Australian studio behind Hollow Knight and Hollow Knight: Silksong announced the stream on November 25, according to GGRecon.
The showcase premieres on YouTube at 7am Pacific, 10am Eastern and 3pm in the UK. Team Cherry says it will bring announcements along with an update on Sea of Sorrow, the free expansion for Silksong.
## What we know about Sea of Sorrow
Sea of Sorrow will be free for everyone who owns Silksong. It adds new areas and new bosses to the game. Team Cherry originally gave it a 2026 release window, which leaves only about five weeks for it to arrive on time.
## What we don't know
The studio hasn't said what the update will be. That leaves several possibilities that fans are already debating: a firm release date, a surprise launch on the day, or a delay into 2027. None of these has been confirmed, so treat any guesses as speculation until the stream airs.
Team Cherry is famous for staying quiet between big reveals. Silksong spent years without a release date before it finally launched, so a dedicated stream from the studio is a rare event. Its timing, the day after Thanksgiving in the US and during the Black Friday sales, also means it will compete with a busy week of deals.
We'll cover what Team Cherry shows on Friday.

articles.title: PlayStation Plus December games: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 and Amnesia: The Bunker
articles.dek: Sony's three Monthly Games for December can be claimed from December 1 to January 4. November's lineup leaves on November 30.
articles.body:
Sony has named the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December. All PS Plus members can add them to their library from Tuesday, December 1 until Monday, January 4, according to the PlayStation Blog. Sony notes that the lineup can vary by region.
## The lineup
- Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 (PS5, PS4): the remake of the third and fourth games in the skating series, with the classic two-minute runs and expanded Create-A-Skater and Create-A-Park tools.
- Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 (PS5, PS4): the anime fighting RPG, including its online multiplayer and Raid Battles.
- Amnesia: The Bunker (PS4): a first-person horror game set during the First World War, in which you play a French soldier trapped in a bunker with something hunting him.
The skating remake is the headline pick. It came out in 2025 and is one of the more recent games to arrive in the Essential tier this year. Xenoverse 2 is much older but still has an active online community, and The Bunker is a well-reviewed horror game that plays on PS5 through backward compatibility.
## Last call for November
November's games, Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Monster Train 2, can still be claimed until Monday, November 30. Once you add a game to your library, it stays playable for as long as you keep a PS Plus subscription.

articles.title: EA Sports FC 27 brings back late commentator John Motson with an AI-recreated voice
articles.dek: An FC 27 update adds the BBC's 'Motty' as an optional commentator, built from his old recordings and AI. His family backs it; some fans call it bleak.
facts: About 10 years of in-game recordings plus AI tools
Son Fred Motson called it a tribute
Undisclosed sum to the family, per the BBC
articles.body:
EA Sports FC 27 is adding John Motson as a commentator three years after his death. The update uses a mix of his original audio and an AI recreation of his voice, according to PC Gamer.
Motson was the BBC's best-known football commentator for decades and died in 2023 at the age of 77. He was also the voice of EA's football games from FIFA Soccer 96 into the mid-2000s.
## How EA built it
EA says it used almost 10 years of Motson's in-game recordings together with new AI tools to create the commentary. That lets the game produce lines he never recorded, such as the names of current players and clubs.
His son, Fred Motson, described it as a touching tribute and told the BBC that his father would have wanted it. The BBC reports that EA paid the family an undisclosed sum for the rights.
## Mixed reaction
PC Gamer reports that reaction among fans has been split. Some welcomed hearing a familiar voice again. Others called the idea disrespectful and bleak, objecting to new lines being put in the mouth of someone who can't approve them.
The move lands in the middle of a wider fight over AI voices in games. Performers and their unions have pushed for consent and pay rules for digital replicas, and EA has reportedly already used AI to generate some lines for living FC commentators who agreed to it. A deceased voice licensed through an estate is a newer and more sensitive case, and it is likely to come up again as other publishers look at their own archives.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Rise is now on iOS and Android through Netflix Games
articles.dek: Capcom's 2021 hunting game is free for Netflix subscribers on phones and tablets, with touch controls and former DLC quests included.
articles.body:
Monster Hunter Rise has arrived on phones and tablets as part of Netflix Games. The mobile version launched on iOS and Android on November 24 and is included for Netflix subscribers at no extra cost, according to PocketGamer.biz.
Rise first came out on Nintendo Switch in 2021 and later reached PC, PlayStation and Xbox. It is one of the biggest console games Netflix has added to its mobile library so far.
## What's different on mobile
- Touch controls have been adapted from the console version.
- A new recovery button automatically picks the best healing item during a fight.
- Quests that used to be paid or time-limited DLC are included as permanent content.
## A crowded mobile year for the series
Rise is the third way to hunt monsters on a phone right now. Niantic's former game Monster Hunter Now, now run by Scopely, has added monsters from Rise, and Monster Hunter Outlanders from TiMi Studio Group launched in October as a mobile-only game.
For Netflix, the release continues a push to bring well-known console games to its subscription service.

articles.title: GTA VI has no story mission replay, so players are leaning on its 15 save slots
articles.dek: The pause-menu replay option from GTA IV's expansion and GTA V is gone, along with gold-medal challenges. Manual saves are the only way back.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't let you replay story missions once you've finished them. Players who want to go back to a favorite mission need to have made a manual save before it, according to Engadget and Insider Gaming.
## A feature that's been around since 2009
Mission replay first appeared in The Ballad of Gay Tony, the 2009 expansion for GTA IV, and returned in GTA V through the pause menu. GTA V also added bronze, silver and gold medals for optional objectives in each mission, which gave players a reason to replay. Neither the replay option nor the medals are in GTA VI.
Engadget reports that GamesRadar's editor-in-chief found no replay option after more than 100 hours, and other reviewers with early access said the same. Insider Gaming, citing IGN, says the reason is that choices you make change how missions and some random events play out, which a simple replay menu would undo.
## How to work around it
GTA VI offers 15 manual save slots, and it has more than 90 main missions. That means you can't keep a save before every mission, so players are choosing which ones to bookmark.
Plenty of content can still be repeated, including races, stunts, pool and other minigames, shop robberies and bank jobs.
Rockstar hasn't said whether it might add a replay option in a later patch.

articles.title: Rockstar's UK staff vote three to one against recognizing the IWGB union
articles.dek: In a ballot that overlapped GTA VI's launch, 1,163 of 1,544 voting employees said no to formal recognition. The union says it will keep organizing.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games employees in the UK have voted against formally recognizing a union. The two-week ballot closed on November 26, and about three in four staff who took part said no to a recognition deal with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union, according to VGC, IGN and Engadget.
IGN reports that 1,544 employees across Rockstar's UK studios in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London cast a vote, a turnout of 93.2%. Of those, 1,163 voted against and 381 voted in favor. Recognition would have made it the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, IGN says.
## What recognition would have meant
A recognition agreement would have given the union a formal framework to negotiate with management on pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, pensions, and how AI and redundancies affect staff, according to VGC. Without it, Rockstar isn't obliged to hold regular meetings with union representatives. Staff can still join the IWGB, and the union can still represent individual members.
## Both sides respond
Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar's head of publishing, said in a statement that the company was proud of its team and the GTA VI launch, and that the result showed staff support for keeping direct relationships and open dialogue with management. Before the vote she had told Bloomberg that Rockstar would follow the team's wishes either way.
The union said hundreds of workers had backed it and that the result was a reason to push harder, not to retreat. It says it will keep campaigning for pay transparency, paid overtime written into contracts, and protections against AI and layoffs.
## The tribunal is still open
The vote came a year after Rockstar dismissed a group of UK staff in 2025. Reports put the number at 31 or 34. The IWGB says the firings were union busting and unlawful. Rockstar says the staff leaked confidential information. An employment tribunal has heard closing arguments, and a judgment hasn't been issued yet.

articles.title: Ubisoft says its games aren't required to use generative AI after a report on pitch rules
articles.dek: Ubisoft staff reportedly have to explain how a new game would use generative AI, or why it won't. The publisher says the choice stays with each team.
facts: Pitches must cover gen AI use or justify skipping it
articles.body:
Ubisoft says its game projects don't have to use generative AI, responding to a report that teams pitching new games must explain how they would use the technology or justify leaving it out.
## What was reported
The report came from Vertical Slice, which spoke to several current Ubisoft employees who weren't named. According to that reporting, new pitch rules ask teams to address generative AI directly: either lay out how the game would use it or explain why it wouldn't. Pitches that address neither would reportedly not get the go-ahead. One source said the company wasn't explicitly forcing teams to use AI, but that leadership's enthusiasm left staff feeling pressured to include it.
## Ubisoft's answer
In a statement carried by several outlets, Ubisoft said it encourages teams to explore AI tools but that projects aren't required to use generative AI, and that each team decides what fits its game.
The report lands days after Ubisoft's half-year results, which included a €254.5 million loss and a plan to spin its generative AI work into a separate studio. Chief executive Yves Guillemot has repeatedly described generative AI as a major shift for the industry, and the company has been hiring for AI-related roles across its studios. Game workers' unions in Europe have pushed back on that direction, calling for limits on how the technology is used in development.

articles.title: Ubisoft tells a court that calling Skull and Bones 'AAAA' was just puffery
articles.dek: A player who sued under Kansas consumer law says the label misled buyers. Ubisoft's lawyers reportedly argue it was hype, not a promise.
facts: Deceptive marketing under Kansas consumer protection law
articles.body:
Ubisoft's lawyers have argued in court that describing Skull and Bones as a "AAAA" game was marketing hype rather than a promise about quality, according to Game File's reporting as covered by Game World Observer and 80.lv.
## Where the label came from
Ubisoft chief executive Yves Guillemot used the term during a Q&A on an earnings call in February 2024, while explaining why the pirate game cost $70. Skull and Bones had spent more than a decade in development. It launched to a lukewarm reception, and its price was cut within weeks, 80.lv notes.
## The lawsuit
Player Jacob Himberger sued Ubisoft in 2025 under Kansas consumer protection law, arguing the AAAA label misled buyers. He asks for compensation for everyone who bought the game, and his complaint lists potential penalties of up to $10,000 for each of several alleged violations, according to 80.lv. He also argues Ubisoft suggested buyers owned the game when they only received a license to play it.
Ubisoft's response, as reported, is that the wording was "classic puffery": broad, boastful language that makes no specific claim, which consumer law generally doesn't punish. It isn't known how Ubisoft answered the ownership argument.
80.lv reports that the case has moved between courts, with a Kansas federal court transferring it to California. The outlets haven't reported a ruling on Ubisoft's argument.

articles.title: Showa American Story is delayed to October 28, 2027
articles.dek: Nekcom's zombie-filled 1980s action RPG was due in 2026. The studio says the core game is finished and the extra time is for polish and optimization.
articles.body:
Showa American Story, the action RPG from Chinese studio Nekcom Entertainment, now launches on October 28, 2027 for PlayStation 5 and PC. Nekcom announced the new date on its X account, and Game Informer and RPG Site reported it.
The game had been due in 2026, and Game Informer notes that the lack of news as the year wound down had already made that look unlikely.
## Content complete, polish to come
Nekcom says the core content of the game is done and that the next eleven months will go into polishing and optimizing it. It's the second delay for the game, which was pushed from 2025 into 2026 last year.
## What it is
Showa American Story is set in an alternate 1980s where a Japanese-flavored America has been overrun by zombies and monsters. You play as Choko, who comes back from the dead and fights through the wreckage with melee weapons, guns and vehicles. Its demo was one of Game Informer's favorite action games at Gamescom.
The game is published by 4Divinity and is listed on Steam with the new date.

articles.title: Unofficial GTA VI PC ports reportedly have multiplayer running
articles.dek: A port tracker says a private group has players, cars and voice chat working at 25 to 30fps, built on the leaked Xbox code. Rockstar hasn't commented.
articles.body:
Fan projects trying to run Grand Theft Auto VI on PC now reportedly have a basic form of multiplayer working, GamesRadar reports. None of this is official, and Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version or an online mode for GTA VI.
## What's being claimed
PortWatch, a tracker that follows unofficial port efforts, posted late on November 26 that multiplayer was running on PC and said it had checked that the video was genuine. The build comes from a private group working on its own fork of an existing port. It reportedly shows several players, cars and proximity voice chat at a steady 25 to 30 frames per second. PortWatch's own tracker puts the overall effort at 91.3% of the way to a working game, a figure that can't be checked independently.
GamesRadar is clear that this is a long way from a full online mode. There are no missions or progression, just players sharing the same space.
## Built on leaked code
The ports trace back to the hacker group Cyberleek, which claimed last week to be leaking a GTA VI development build and released an executable from the Xbox version. Port groups have been working from that code since. VideoCardz reports that mods may be starting to appear too.
The ports rely on leaked material and are almost certain to face legal action. At least one high-profile project has already gone through an apparent Discord takedown. Rockstar hasn't responded to the reports, and GTA VI is still only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
